chemistrySummary.value: Amoxicillin is an aminopenicillin with a beta-lactam ring that targets bacterial cell-wall synthesis machinery.

moaSummary.value: It binds penicillin-binding proteins, blocking peptidoglycan cross-linking so growing bacteria cannot maintain a stable cell wall.

discoveryNote.value: Developed as a broader-spectrum oral penicillin derivative to improve absorption versus earlier penicillins.

chemistrySummary.value: Combination of amoxicillin with clavulanic acid, a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects the penicillin from enzymatic breakdown.

moaSummary.value: Amoxicillin inhibits cell-wall synthesis; clavulanate inactivates many beta-lactamases so the antibiotic remains active against resistant strains.
Inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis via penicillin-binding proteins; spectrum narrower than aminopenicillins.
Penicillinase-stable penicillin used primarily against staphylococci; still a cell-wall synthesis inhibitor.
Beta-lactam cephalosporin that inhibits peptidoglycan cross-linking in susceptible bacteria.
Second-generation cephalosporin cell-wall synthesis inhibitor with broader Gram-negative coverage than first-generation agents.
Parenteral third-generation cephalosporin inhibiting bacterial cell-wall synthesis; often reserved for more serious infections.
Macrolide that binds the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis.
Macrolide inhibiting protein synthesis at the 50S ribosomal subunit; notable CYP3A4 interaction potential (clinical details pending sourced publish).
Classic macrolide that blocks bacterial protein synthesis at the 50S subunit.
Tetracycline that binds the 30S ribosomal subunit and inhibits protein synthesis. Dairy/divalent cations can chelate oral doses — counselling detail pending full sourced publish.
Fluoroquinolone that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase / topoisomerase IV, blocking DNA replication.
Nitroimidazole activated in anaerobic organisms to reactive products that damage microbial DNA.
Sequential blockade of folate synthesis: sulfamethoxazole inhibits dihydropteroate synthase; trimethoprim inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
Urinary antiseptic activated inside bacteria to reactive intermediates that damage multiple macromolecules.
Lincosamide that binds the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits protein synthesis.
Glycopeptide that binds D-Ala-D-Ala termini of peptidoglycan precursors, blocking cell-wall synthesis in Gram-positive organisms.
Aminoglycoside that binds the 30S ribosomal subunit, causing misreading of mRNA and bactericidal effect in susceptible organisms.
Oxazolidinone that prevents formation of the 70S initiation complex, inhibiting protein synthesis.
Inhibits bacterial dihydrofolate reductase, blocking tetrahydrofolate production needed for nucleic acid synthesis.

lessons.title: The Story
lessons.body: Amoxicillin was developed to improve oral absorption versus earlier penicillins — a practical win for outpatient infection treatment.

lessons.title: Chemical Structure
lessons.body: Tap the beta-lactam ring in your mind: that four-membered ring is the business end that blocks cell-wall builders.

lessons.title: Mechanism of Action
lessons.body: Bacteria build a brick wall (peptidoglycan). Amoxicillin stops the bricklayers. Wall fails → cell bursts when it tries to grow.

lessons.title: Inside the Body
lessons.body: ADME journey scaffold: swallowed → absorbed → distributed → works at infection site → cleared (kidney-focused for many penicillins). Details pending sourced PK publish.

lessons.title: Clinical Pearls
lessons.body: Allergy history is the first counselling question. Cell wall ≠ ribosome — that distinction wins exam marks and safer dispensing.

quiz.teachFromMiss: You're thinking of macrolides (50S), fluoroquinolones (gyrase), or antifolates. Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam — cell wall.

lessons.title: The Story
lessons.body: Clavulanate was added so amoxicillin could keep working when bacteria make beta-lactamase enzymes that would otherwise destroy the penicillin.

lessons.title: Chemical Structure
lessons.body: Two partners: the aminopenicillin (cell-wall attack) plus a beta-lactamase inhibitor (shield).

lessons.title: Mechanism of Action
lessons.body: Amoxicillin blocks wall building; clavulanate occupies and inactivates many beta-lactamases — a bodyguard, not the main fighter.

lessons.title: Inside the Body
lessons.body: Same oral pathway as amoxicillin for many products; ratio and salt form matter for which SKU you dispense — check the brand dossier.

lessons.title: Clinical Pearls
lessons.body: In SA, Augmentin is the originator brand many patients know — resolve brand → molecule first, then counsel on allergy history.

quiz.prompt: Clavulanate’s main job in the combination is to…
choices: Kill bacteria by blocking the 30S ribosome
quiz.teachFromMiss: Clavulanate is the shield — it disables beta-lactamases so amoxicillin can still hit the cell wall.

lessons.title: The Story
lessons.body: Tetracyclines opened a different attack surface — protein synthesis — useful when beta-lactams are not the right tool.

lessons.title: Chemical Structure
lessons.body: A four-ring tetracycline core; chelation with metals is the structural reason dairy and antacids matter for absorption counselling.

lessons.title: Mechanism of Action
lessons.body: Binds the 30S ribosomal subunit and stalls protein synthesis — not a cell-wall drug.

lessons.title: Inside the Body
lessons.body: Oral absorption can drop if taken with divalent cations (calcium, iron, antacids). Counselling timing is the practical pearl.

lessons.title: Clinical Pearls
lessons.body: Exam trap: ‘take with milk’ is often wrong for doxycycline because of chelation — spot-the-error gold.

lessons.title: The Story
lessons.body: Built for organisms that thrive without oxygen — activated inside them into reactive damage.

lessons.title: Chemical Structure
lessons.body: A nitroimidazole; the nitro group is the fuse that anaerobic metabolism lights.

lessons.title: Mechanism of Action
lessons.body: Reduced inside anaerobes to reactive products that damage microbial DNA.

lessons.title: Inside the Body
lessons.body: Widely distributed; alcohol interaction counselling is a classic counter pearl (details pending sourced publish for specific guidance).

lessons.title: Clinical Pearls
lessons.body: Think anaerobes and protozoa when you see metronidazole on a script — then check the published counselling points.

quiz.prompt: Metronidazole is best remembered as acting via…
quiz.teachFromMiss: Nitroimidazoles are activated in anaerobic environments and damage DNA — different story from beta-lactams or tetracyclines.
